name: Coxeter plane and Petrie polygon projections of polytopes
summary: A Petrie polygon of a regular polyhedron follows edges such that every consecutive pair, but no consecutive triple, belongs to one face. Every finite regular polytope admits an orthogonal planar projection making one Petrie polygon a regular polygon. The associated Coxeter plane is preserved by a Coxeter element acting as a rotation.
source_title: Discrete Groups Generated by Reflections — H. S. M. Coxeter, 1934, pp. 604–605
caveat: The projection statement requires a finite regular polytope and a specially selected plane; arbitrary sampled rotations are not Coxeter-plane construction. This runtime only samples Givens rotations, measures polar angular gaps, rotates a phi-scaled second shape, and compares catalog targets. It does not implement Coxeter planes, exhaustive grand-tour convergence, projection pursuit, Penrose construction, or a principal-angle solver. Angular coincidences cannot establish natural causes.
